overall: The AG let the committees keep withholding the October 29, 2009 minutes, declined to review privilege claims, and found the January 24, 2011 NSC minutes too thin and missing a document list, ordering a complete rewrite within 60 days.

allegations.summary: Complaint asked whether the collective bargaining purpose for withholding the October 29, 2009 executive session minutes had expired and the minutes must be released.
allegations.key_passage: We have reviewed the unredacted October 29, 2009 executive session minutes, in camera, and have determined that the executive session purpose has not yet expired.

allegations.summary: Complaint asked whether the strategy purpose for withholding the October 7, 2010 executive session minutes had expired, requiring their release.
allegations.key_passage: This executive session purpose appears to have expired, therefore, necessitating the Committees' review of the October 7, 2010 minutes and release of those minutes

allegations.summary: Complaint asked the AG to review minutes and documents withheld or redacted under attorney/client privilege to determine whether they contain true legal advice.
allegations.key_passage: Based on the information provided, we have no reason to challenge the Committees' claim of attorney/client privilege.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged minutes of the November 13, 2009, February 23, 2010 and other pre-July 2010 executive sessions lacked sufficient detail.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore decline to review whether minutes from meetings that occurred prior to July 1, 2010 contain sufficient detail.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the November 4, 2010 joint executive session minutes failed to identify the members who spoke.
allegations.key_passage: The minutes do not need to identify each speaker, so long as a member of the public can read the minutes and understand from the summary the nature of the discussion and how the public body arrived at its decisions.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the January 24, 2011 NSC executive session minutes lacked sufficient detail of the proposal, counter-offer and strategy discussion.
allegations.key_passage: A member of the public cannot read those few sentences and understand what occurred over the course of the three and one-half hour meeting.

allegations.summary: The January 24, 2011 NSC executive session minutes did not include a list of the documents used at the meeting, as the law requires.
allegations.key_passage: The minutes from the NSC's January 24, 2011 meeting failed to include a list of the documents used by the Committees.

allegations.summary: Complaint sought release of documents on the committees' financial assessments of the approved AEA contract, which were not used at an open meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Such requests must be directed to the Secretary of State's Public Records Division, which enforces the Commonwealth's Public Records Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law by the Committees.
The Negotiating Subcommittee must create and approve complete minutes of its January 24, 2011 meeting within sixty (60) days of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Committees' immediate and future compliance with the law, and order the NSC to create and approve complete minutes of its January 24, 2011 meeting within sixty (60) days of receipt of this letter.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
